tagline: Through forest and river valleys, across the divide at St. Marys
intro: The Bucktail Trail follows Pennsylvania Route 120 between Ridgway and Lock Haven, through the Sproul and Elk State Forests. Pennsylvania Wilds describes a 100-mile byway with West Branch Susquehanna views and seven state parks within reach. Near Renovo, the road winds through mountains beside the river. The state byway designation took effect January 6, 2004.

Before it became PA 120, the highway was U.S. Route 120, planned in 1926 to connect Erie and Philadelphia but shortened to Ridgway–Reading in 1927. That designation followed an earlier effort to recognize the valley landscape. In 1933, Pennsylvania’s legislature established the Bucktail State Park Natural Area along 75 miles between Emporium and Lock Haven. Its boundaries extend from mountain rim to mountain rim, and include both state forest and private land. The Bucktail name honors the Civil War regiment drawn from this region.

Begin at Ridgway, in the Clarion River valley, and head east toward St. Marys, whose downtown straddles the Eastern Continental Divide. Beyond St. Marys, Route 120 reaches Emporium and follows the Driftwood Branch southeast to Driftwood. There the Bennett Branch joins the Driftwood Branch; the road continues downstream along Sinnemahoning Creek and the West Branch to Renovo. From Renovo, the river leads the drive southeast to Lock Haven.

moments.title: St. Marys
moments.text: Water leaving downtown St. Marys has two very different destinations. The Eastern Continental Divide runs directly through it: drainage on the eastern side reaches the Atlantic, while water to the west reaches the Gulf of Mexico. Founded in 1842, the settlement was inhabited mostly by Bavarian Roman Catholics. In 1992 the borough absorbed surrounding Benzinger Township and became a city. That merger explains its extensive boundaries: most of the city’s land is unurbanized, with trout streams and state hunting lands inside the city limits. Its economic history also reaches beyond farming and lumber: carbon graphite manufacturers expanded here during the twentieth century.

moments.title: Driftwood
moments.text: At Driftwood, two branches meet beneath the Allegheny Plateau. The creek and its tributaries have cut a gorge 1,200 feet deep or more, with the community at the bottom. The borough takes its name from the Driftwood Branch of Sinnemahoning Creek. Route 120 follows that branch from Emporium, then continues downstream beside Sinnemahoning Creek toward the West Branch Susquehanna and Renovo. The other valley leads west: Route 555 follows the Bennett Branch toward Weedville.

moments.title: Renovo
moments.text: Great Lakes names on the avenues and numbered side streets give Renovo the plan of an industrial town. The Philadelphia & Erie Railroad built it as the midpoint of its line, on a mostly flat floodplain beside the West Branch Susquehanna. Houses stood close together, including rows of attached homes. The Philadelphia and Erie line eventually became part of the Pennsylvania Railroad, which was the town’s major employer. The railroad shops serviced steam and diesel locomotives and had their own coal power plant. Those shops closed in the 1960s. The town occupies a gorge 1,000 to 1,200 feet deep.
moments.notice: The avenues carry Great Lakes names; the side streets are numbered from 1 to 16.
